props.title: Slumber Party Massacre III

sections.content: The third entry in the Slumber Party Massacre series continues the franchise's unique position as horror films initially conceived as feminist parodies but executed as straight slashers. While less critically acclaimed than Slumber Party Massacre (1982), which was penned by feminist activist Rita Mae Brown, this 1990 installment follows similar beats while amping up the gratuitous elements. It sits alongside other late-80s/early-90s slashers like Sleepaway Camp III (1989) and Friday the 13th Part VIII (1989) in representing the final gasps of the golden age slasher era before Scream (1996) revolutionized the genre.

sections.content: The film's placement in horror history is particularly interesting as it represents the tail end of the direct-to-video slasher boom. Like Silent Night, Deadly Night 3 (1989) and Cheerleader Camp (1988), it demonstrates how the subgenre had become formulaic by 1990, relying heavily on established tropes while adding little innovation. The drill-wielding killer concept, while a clear phallic metaphor in the original film's feminist framework, becomes more straightforwardly exploitative here. SUBHEAD: Evolution of the Female-Centered Slasher

What sets the Slumber Party Massacre series apart is its female creative involvement, with the original directed by Amy Holden Jones and the sequel by Deborah Brock. While the third entry had male director Sally Mattison, it still maintains some of the series' examination of female perspectives in horror, albeit less overtly. This positions it alongside other female-gaze horror films like Lady in White (1988) and Pet Sematary (1989), though with considerably less artistic ambition.
